label: achiever (VALS)
source_text: Wikipedia, 'VALS' § Segments (citing SBI's 'US Framework and VALS Types'): "These consumers are the high-resource group of those who are motivated by achievement. They are successful work-oriented people who get their satisfaction from their jobs and families." Textbook rendering of SBI's segment text (Brainscape flashcards): "has goal-oriented lifestyles that center on family and career. They avoid situation that encourage a high degree of stimulation or change." Umbrex summary: "Goal-oriented, career and family focused; favor premium, time-saving, and status-affirming offerings; prefer established, success-signaling brands."
description_draft: This means living a goal-oriented life centered on career and family, taking one's satisfaction from work and home, avoiding upheaval, and buying established prestige brands that show one's success to peers.
nearest_existing: ambitious / career_oriented / status_seeking: the typed version is a settled, conventional high earner whose success-signalling is in what he buys (prestige brands, time-savers) and who avoids upheaval; ambitious is the drive itself, career_oriented the priority, status_seeking the motive without the settled family-and-work life or the consumer habits.
notes: Canonical page https://www.strategicbusinessinsights.com/vals/ustypes/achievers.shtml could not be fetched today: the host does not resolve (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND, with and without www) and web.archive.org is blocked for this tool. Fallback: Wikipedia's segment lines (which cite the SBI page) plus a textbook rendering and secondary summaries, all fetched (https://brainscape.com/flashcards/chapter-12-9893250/packs/17243429, https://umbrex.com/?p=241479, https://thinkinsights.net/consulting/vals-framework, https://slm.mba/?p=1891). SBI's fuller wording ('deep commitment to career and family', 'politically conservative, respect authority and the status quo', 'favor established, prestige products and services that demonstrate success to their peers') is known but not quoted, because no page carrying it could be fetched. Strength: neutral-to-flattering portrait of a conventional striver-made-good; milder than the corpus's plain ambitious.
set_review: Eight members, one grain: primary motivation (ideals: thinker, believer; achievement: achiever, striver; self-expression: experiencer, maker; innovator above and survivor below the three), the person's outlook, then how they buy, in that order, 29 to 32 words each, all 'This means being/living/leading ...'. Resources read off the pairs (thinker/believer, achiever/striver, experiencer/maker): the high-resource member has the ample means, the low-resource member is 'of modest means', 'ahead of one's money', 'on the fewest means'. The source is consumer-segment text, so every draft ends with buying habits; VALS is a marketing typology and the buying clause is what tells a thinker from a believer. SBI's own pages could not be fetched today (host does not resolve; Wayback blocked), so every member is drafted from Wikipedia's segment lines (which cite the SBI page) plus fetched secondary renderings of SBI's wording; SBI's fuller sentences are noted per entry where I know them but could not source them, and search-engine snippets confirmed several of them without a fetchable page. Roger should expect to recheck these eight against the SBI pages when they are reachable. Strength: the high-resource portraits (innovator, thinker, achiever, experiencer) are flattering by design; striver and survivor are gently unflattering; all are milder than the corpus's plain traits except experiencer, which is about as strong as the plain impulsive/spontaneous and is the member nearest a plain corpus trait.

label: acts of service
source_text: "Anything you do to ease the burden of responsibilities weighing on an 'Acts of Service' person will speak volumes. The words they most want to hear: 'Let me do that for you.' Laziness, broken commitments, and making more work for them tell speakers of this love language their feelings don't matter. Finding ways to serve speaks volumes to the recipient of these acts."
description_draft: This means feeling loved by help that lightens one's load, longing to hear 'let me do that for you', while laziness, broken commitments and extra work say one's feelings don't matter.
nearest_existing: helpful / supportive / transactional: those are about giving; this is about how one receives love, the help one wants done for oneself and the sting when it is withheld. No corpus trait is about the channel through which affection is felt.
notes: The official /learn page (https://5lovelanguages.com/learn) now carries a one-liner per language ('For these people, actions speak louder than words.'); the full official paragraphs survive on the site's quiz-results pages, which is the URL recorded (every results page carries all five). Strength: Chapman's text is warm and its 'hurt' clause is a want, not a vice; comparable in weight to a mild corpus trait.
set_review: Five members, one grain and one shape: 'This means feeling loved through/by X: what delights, while what wounds', 30 to 32 words each, all written for the person who receives love this way (Chapman's text addresses 'you'; rendered in the corpus's one-form). Each is told from the others by the channel and by its specific wound (an insult; distraction; a forgotten birthday; broken commitments; neglect). Source is the official site's full paragraphs on a quiz-results page, since /learn now has one-liners. The source is pre-balanced, each delight paired with a hurt, so strength mirrors it at the corpus's mild-to-middling level; none is flattering in the Hogwarts sense. 'Receiving gifts' keeps the source's 'not materialism' defence as 'treasured for the thought and effort'. Trademark symbols and the system's name are left out.

label: auditory (VARK)
source_text: "The Aural mode describes a preference for information that is 'heard or spoken.'" Learners with this preference "learn best from lectures, group discussions, radio, email, messaging, podcasts, speaking, and talking things through." The preference "includes talking out loud as well as talking to oneself." Often these learners "want to sort things out by speaking first, rather than sorting out their ideas and then speaking."
description_draft: This means learning best from what is heard or spoken: lectures, group discussion, radio, podcasts and talking things through, aloud or to oneself, and often sorting out one's ideas by speaking first.
nearest_existing: stream_of_consciousness / gregarious: the typed version is a learning channel, the preference for hearing and saying over seeing and reading, with no claim about sociability or style of expression; nothing in the corpus is about how one takes information in.
notes: VARK's own name for this modality is 'Aural'; the queue label says 'auditory' and is kept as given. The source's 'often' is kept as 'often'. Strength: neutral and descriptive, like the whole VARK set; weaker than any plain corpus trait.
set_review: Four members, one grain: the channel ('what is heard or spoken', 'written words', 'maps, diagrams, charts', 'real-life experience'), then the typical materials from Fleming's own lists, 30 to 32 words each, all 'This means learning best from / taking in information as ...'. Visual keeps the source's explicit exclusion (not photographs or video) as a 'rather than' clause because 'visual' is polysemous and the exclusion picks the sense; it is the only 'rather than' in the set. Fleming's text is neutral; no member is flattering, and all four are weaker than the corpus's plain traits, which is expected of a learning-preference instrument. The label 'auditory' is the queue's; VARK says 'Aural'. This set supersedes the visual-thinker / verbal-thinker pair from part 3 (dropped per the queue decision).

label: believer (VALS)
source_text: Wikipedia 'VALS' § Segments: "These consumers are the low-resource group of those who are motivated by ideals. They are conservative and predictable consumers who favor local products and established brands." Textbook rendering (Brainscape): "are strongly traditional and respect rules and authority. Because they are fundamentally conservative, they are slow to change and technology averse." slm.mba summary: "loyal and predictable consumers, rooted in family, community, and moral principles".
description_draft: This means being a conservative, conventional person of modest means, rooted in family, community and moral principles, respecting rules and authority, slow to change, and buying predictably: familiar products and established brands.
nearest_existing: traditional / conservative / brand_loyal / rule_abiding: the typed version bundles all four in one settled, modest-means life organised around home, community and faith, with the buying habit as its tell; traditional is the value alone, brand_loyal the habit alone.
notes: SBI page unreachable today (see achiever notes). SBI's fuller text names 'family, religion, community, and the nation' and 'favor American products'; not quoted for want of a fetchable page. Strength: mildly flattering (steady, loyal) with 'slow to change' as its one shadow; milder than the corpus's conservative.

label: blood type A
source_text: Wikipedia, 'Blood type personality theory', lead: "people with type A blood are friendly and kind but also obsessive and anxious". Supplement, Voyapon 'Blood types in Japan' (Y. Tanaka, 2026): "people with blood type A are said to be self-sacrificing and down-to-earth individuals, characterized by diligence, creativity, and sensitivity." "this blood type is thought to be orderly and punctual (几帳面な, kichoumenna) as well as detail-oriented (細かい, komakai)."
description_draft: This means being friendly, kind, down-to-earth and self-sacrificing, diligent, orderly and punctual, attentive to detail and sensitive to others, but also anxious and obsessive.
nearest_existing: conscientious / anxious / meticulous: the typed version is the folk bundle of all three in one person, virtues first, faults after; conscientious has no anxiety, anxious no diligence.
notes: Wikipedia's current article gives one clause per type in the lead and no trait table (the raw wikitext was checked); the fuller conventional portrait is taken from Voyapon (https://voyapon.com/blood-types-in-japan/), a travel magazine, with the Japanese terms. Voyapon's 'creativity' is dropped because Wikipedia assigns creative to type B. Strength: balanced, as the source; about the corpus's level.
set_review: Four members, one grain and shape: virtues first, then 'but also' and the faults, 24 to 29 words, all 'This means being ...'. The set keeps the folk balance Wikipedia reports (every type has a but-clause); AB is the only one defined relationally ('combining opposing traits') and keeps 'mysterious or aloof', which Wikipedia ties to the type's rarity in Japan. Wikipedia, the packet's source of record, is thin (one clause per type, no table), so each entry supplements it from Voyapon's 2026 guide with the Japanese terms; the Korean variant is not separately sourced. Wikipedia notes that the minority types B and AB are more negatively stereotyped, and the drafts mirror that (B's fault list is the longest). The theory's scientific status (superstition) is not the description's business. Strength: at the corpus's level, neither flattering nor harsh.

label: blood type AB
source_text: Wikipedia lead: "those with type AB are a mix of stereotypical A and B traits, while also being seen as mysterious or aloof due to their relatively low population in Japan." Voyapon: "People with this blood type are characterized as extremely ambivalent, as they combine opposing traits." "they are said to be very changeable and fluctuating in nature, while also possessing a strongly analytical and critical mind." "They are also attributed a certain degree of eccentricity (風変わり, fuugawari) and rationality (合理的, gouriteki)."
description_draft: This means combining opposing traits: kind and careful yet spontaneous and creative, changeable in mood, rational, analytical and critical, somewhat eccentric, and seen by others as mysterious or aloof.
nearest_existing: mercurial / enigmatic / analytical: the typed version is the folk mix, a changeable, rational, somewhat eccentric person others find hard to read; mercurial is the mood swing alone, enigmatic the opacity alone.
notes: 'Kind and careful yet spontaneous and creative' renders 'a mix of A and B traits' without naming the sibling types, using Wikipedia's own A and B adjectives. Strength: balanced; the faults (changeable, critical, aloof) are mild.

label: blood type B
source_text: Wikipedia lead: "people with type B are spontaneous and creative but can be selfish". Voyapon: "blood type B individuals are viewed in Japanese society as sociable, extroverted, and optimistic." "they are said to possess a strong self-confidence, which can sometimes take on vain and arrogant traits; according to the blood type theory, this is also interpreted as being selfish (利己的, rikoteki)." "Irresponsibility (無責任, musekinin) is another trait attributed to blood type B individuals."
description_draft: This means being spontaneous, creative and optimistic, sociable, outgoing and sure of oneself, but also irresponsible and at times selfish, with a confidence that sometimes turns vain and arrogant.
nearest_existing: spontaneous / self_assured / selfish / irresponsible: the typed version bundles the lively virtues and these two faults in one portrait; the corpus's spontaneous has no selfishness and its selfish no charm.
notes: Hedges kept as plain words: 'can be selfish' -> 'at times selfish'; 'can sometimes take on' -> 'sometimes turns'. Wikipedia notes B is more negatively stereotyped than A or O; the draft has the longest fault list of the four accordingly. Strength: balanced.

label: blood type O
source_text: Wikipedia lead: "people with type O are confident but stubborn and aggressive." Voyapon: "those with blood type O are also thought to belong to the sociable and extroverted category." "They are said to be good at expressing their opinions in a constructive manner, thereby providing stability and control to those around them." "people with blood type O in Japan are also described as jealous (嫉妬深い, shittobukai) and arrogant (高慢, kouman)."
description_draft: This means being confident, sociable and outgoing, speaking one's mind in a constructive way that steadies the people around one, but also stubborn, aggressive, jealous and arrogant.
nearest_existing: confident / dominant / unyielding: the typed version is the folk 'natural leader', sociable and steadying, with stubbornness, aggression and jealousy as the faults; dominant lacks the warmth, confident the faults.
notes: Strength: balanced; the fault list is as long as the virtue list, mirroring the source.

label: experiencer (VALS)
source_text: Wikipedia 'VALS' § Segments: "These consumers are the high-resource group of those who are motivated by self-expression. They are the youngest of all the segments, with a median age of 25." Textbook rendering (Brainscape): "appreciate the unconventional. They are active and impulsive, seeking stimulation from the new, offbeat, and risky." slm.mba: "young, enthusiastic, and energetic consumers with relatively high resources. They love trying new things". Umbrex: "Young-minded, novelty-seeking, impulsive; spend on experiences, fashion, and new products".
description_draft: This means being young, enthusiastic, active and impulsive, loving the unconventional, seeking stimulation in whatever is new, offbeat or risky, and spending freely on fashion, new things and experiences.
nearest_existing: risk_seeking / spontaneous / early_adopter / hedonistic: the typed version is the young self-expresser who buys excitement; closest to the plain impulsive-and-adventurous cluster and about as strong, which makes it the VALS member least distinct from the plain corpus.
notes: SBI page unreachable today. SBI's own 'quickly become enthusiastic about new possibilities but are equally quick to cool' and 'savoring the new, the offbeat, and the risky' appeared in search-engine snippets but on no fetchable page, so they are not quoted or drafted in. Strength: flattering-lively; about the corpus's level.

label: Gryffindor
source_text: Wizarding World, 'What does your Hogwarts house say about you?' (2021-04-28): "Gryffindor house is where you would find the pluckiest and most daring students"; qualities "courage, bravery and determination"; the type of person who "likes to stand up for the little guy, challenges authority, has a tendency to act first and think later". Official fact file: Godric Gryffindor "favoured students who possessed characteristics such as courage, bravery and determination". Wikipedia 'Hogwarts': Gryffindor "values courage, nerve, and chivalry". The Sorting Hat's "dwell the brave at heart" is quoted on the official 'house animal and colours' feature.
description_draft: This means being brave, plucky, daring and determined, with the nerve and chivalry to stand up for the little guy and challenge authority, and a tendency to act first and think later.
nearest_existing: brave / bold / reckless: the typed version is the house portrait, courage plus chivalry (standing up for the little guy) plus the shadow of acting before thinking; brave alone lacks the chivalry and the shadow, reckless lacks the courage's nobility.
notes: Fandom (harrypotter.fandom.com) returns HTTP 402 to this tool and Wikiquote does not carry the Sorting Hat's song, so the song is represented only by the phrases the official site quotes (https://www.harrypotter.com/features/what-your-hogwarts-house-animal-and-colours-could-mean; fact file https://www.harrypotter.com/fact-file/magical-miscellany/gryffindor; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hogwarts). The 2021 feature's jokier items ('class clown', 'takes board games very seriously') are left out. Strength: flattering by design, markedly more so than the corpus's plain brave; the one shadow ('act first and think later') is the source's own.
set_review: Four members, one grain and shape: the house's virtue list (from the official 2021 feature and fact file, agreeing with Wikipedia's one-line values), then two or three characteristic behaviours from the official feature's 'type of person' list, then the shadow where the source gives one, 31 to 32 words, all 'This means being ...'. Shadows: Gryffindor acts first and thinks later; Slytherin never shows the soft side and minds reputation; Ravenclaw is eccentric and dreamy; Hufflepuff has none in the source (humility is a virtue), so it is the only one without. Strength: all four are flattering by design, markedly more than the corpus's plain traits; Slytherin especially, since the official text ('unfortunate reputation', 'possibly destined for greatness') plays down the villainy the books give the house, and the draft mirrors that rather than the Sorting Hat's 'use any means to achieve their ends', which I could not fetch (Fandom 402; Wikiquote lacks the song). Roger may want Slytherin sharpened toward the book; flagged, not done. The playful list items (best snacks, board games) are omitted as not traits.

label: Hufflepuff
source_text: Wizarding World (2021-04-28): "Hufflepuff is where you will find the most trustworthy and hardworking students"; "the most humble of all the houses and don't feel the need to shout about their achievements"; the type of person who "has a strong moral compass, always works hard, is the most loyal friend, knows it is the taking part that counts". Official fact file: Helga Hufflepuff "valued hard work, patience, loyalty and fairness over any particular aptitude"; Hufflepuffs "were actually well known to be kind, reliable and honest." Wikipedia: "values hard work, patience, justice, and loyalty."
description_draft: This means being trustworthy, hardworking and patient, loyal to one's friends, fair and kind, with a strong moral compass, humble about one's achievements, and sure it is the taking part that counts.
nearest_existing: loyal / dependable / industrious / humble: the typed version is all four in one modest, fair-minded worker who prizes taking part over winning; dependable is the reliability alone, loyal the attachment alone.
notes: Only house with no shadow in the source. 'Always has the best snacks' omitted. Fact file: https://www.harrypotter.com/fact-file/magical-miscellany/hufflepuff. Strength: flattering by design, markedly more than the corpus's plain loyal or dependable.

label: innovator (VALS)
source_text: Wikipedia 'VALS' § Segments: "These consumers are on the leading edge of change, have the highest incomes, and such high self-esteem and abundant resources that they can indulge in any or all self-orientations." Textbook rendering (Brainscape): "are successful sophisticate, take-charge people with high self-esteem. They are change leader and are the most receptive to new ideas and technologies." ThinkInsights: "They treat consumption as an expression of taste, independence and character, not as a functional necessity."
description_draft: This means being a successful, sophisticated, take-charge person with high self-esteem and ample means, leading change, taking up new ideas and technologies first, and buying to express cultivated taste and independence.
nearest_existing: early_adopter / self_assured / wealthy / aesthete: the typed version is the high-resource consumer who leads change and buys for taste; early_adopter is the technology habit alone, self_assured the self-esteem alone, without the means or the cultivated taste.
notes: SBI page unreachable today. SBI's own 'purchases reflect cultivated tastes for upscale, niche products and services' is known but not quoted. Strength: the most flattering VALS portrait; markedly more flattering than the corpus's plain confident or early_adopter.

label: kinesthetic (VARK)
source_text: "People with a Kinesthetic preference learn best when ideas are connected to real-life experience." They want to "understand how things work in practice, not just in theory." "Kinesthetic learners are drawn to examples, case studies, demonstrations, simulations, and practical applications." The defining feature is that "information is grounded in reality rather than being abstract or theoretical."
description_draft: This means learning best when ideas are tied to real-life experience, wanting to know how things work in practice, not just theory, and drawn to examples, case studies, demonstrations and practical application.
nearest_existing: hands_on / concrete / practical / experiential: the typed version is a learning channel, the need for a real case before an idea lands; hands_on is a working style, concrete a thinking style, and neither is about how one learns.
notes: Fleming's Kinesthetic is broader than 'learning by moving': it is grounding in real experience, which the draft keeps. 'Simulations' dropped for length. Strength: neutral.

label: maker (VALS)
source_text: Wikipedia 'VALS' § Segments: "These consumers are the low-resource group of those who are motivated by self-expression. They are practical people who value self-sufficiency." Textbook rendering (Brainscape): "value practicality and self-sufficiency. They choose hands-on constructive activities and spend leisure time with family and close friend." slm.mba: "practical, hands-on individuals who express themselves through doing rather than buying". Umbrex: "Practical, self-sufficient; value functionality, durability, and 'do-it-yourself'".
description_draft: This means being a practical, self-sufficient person who expresses oneself through hands-on, do-it-yourself work rather than buying, spending free time with family and close friends, and wanting only functional, durable goods.
nearest_existing: hands_on / self_reliant / practical / frugal: the typed version puts all four into one modest-means life of fixing and building with family around; self_reliant is the independence alone, hands_on the working style alone, frugal the buying alone.
notes: SBI page unreachable today. SBI's own 'suspicious of new ideas and large institutions such as big business' and 'building a house, raising children, fixing a car, or canning vegetables' appeared in search snippets but on no fetchable page, so they are not drafted in; the suspicion of institutions is a real part of the segment that the draft lacks, for Roger to decide. Strength: mildly flattering (capable, down to earth); milder than the corpus's plain traits.

label: physical touch
source_text: "A person whose primary Love Language® is Physical Touch™ is, not surprisingly, very touchy. Hugs, pats on the back, holding hands, and thoughtful touches on the arm, shoulder, or face – they can all be ways to show excitement, concern, care, and love. Physical presence and accessibility are crucial, while neglect or abuse can be unforgivable and destructive. Physical touch fosters a sense of security and belonging in any relationship."
description_draft: This means feeling loved through touch: hugs, a pat on the back, holding hands or a hand on the arm carry care and excitement, physical presence is crucial, and neglect is unforgivable.
nearest_existing: flirty / clingy / emotionally_engaged: none is close; the typed version is the channel of affection, touch, with neglect as its wound, and carries no claim of sexuality or dependence.
notes: 'Can be unforgivable' rendered as 'is unforgivable', the plain-word equivalent for the person who feels it. 'Appropriate' touch, which the site's one-liner stresses, is not a trait and is left out. Strength: as the source, warm with one wound.

label: quality time
source_text: "In the vernacular of Quality Time™, nothing says, 'I love you,' like full, undivided attention. Being there for this type of person is critical, but really being there – with the TV off, fork and knife down, and all chores and tasks on standby – makes your significant other feel truly special and loved. Distractions, postponed dates, or the failure to listen can be especially hurtful. The love language of Quality Time also means sharing quality conversations and quality activities."
description_draft: This means feeling loved through undivided attention: someone really there, screen off and chores set aside, sharing conversation and activities, while distractions, postponed dates or not being listened to are especially hurtful.
nearest_existing: engaged / emotionally_engaged / clingy: the typed version wants the other's full presence and is hurt by distraction; engaged is one's own attention, not the need for another's.
notes: 'TV off' rendered as 'screen off'. 'Can be especially hurtful' -> 'are especially hurtful'. Strength: as the source.

label: Ravenclaw
source_text: Wizarding World (2021-04-28): "If you are looking for the brainiest students – you would find them in Ravenclaw"; the Sorting Hat would put you there only if you showed "excellent wisdom, wit and a skill for learning"; Ravenclaws are "quite eccentric and most of the great wizarding inventors and innovators have come from this house"; the type of person who "analyses everything, is an overachiever, can be described as away with the fairies, is not afraid to be an individual and has a head stuffed full of interesting facts". Official fact file: the house "prized students whose focus was on learning, wit and wisdom." Wikipedia: "values intelligence, learning, wisdom, and wit."
description_draft: This means being a brainy overachiever who prizes wit, wisdom and learning, analyzes everything, keeps a head stuffed with interesting facts, is eccentric and dreamy, and unafraid to be an individual.
nearest_existing: cerebral / erudite / curious / eccentric: the typed version is the house portrait, cleverness prized as a value plus eccentricity and individualism; cerebral is the thinking style alone, erudite the stock of learning alone.
notes: 'Away with the fairies' rendered as 'dreamy'. US spelling 'analyzes'. Fact file: https://www.harrypotter.com/fact-file/magical-miscellany/ravenclaw. Strength: flattering by design, markedly more than the corpus's plain cerebral; the eccentric/dreamy shadow is the source's.

label: read-write (VARK)
source_text: "The Read/write preference is for information displayed as words." This "emphasizes text-based input and output – reading and writing in all its forms, but especially manuals, reports, essays, and assignments." People preferring this modality are "often addicted to PowerPoint, lists, diaries, dictionaries, thesauri, quotations, and words, words, words…"
description_draft: This means taking in and giving out information as written words: reading and writing in every form, especially manuals, reports and essays, and often hooked on lists, diaries, dictionaries and quotations.
nearest_existing: literate / verbose / retentive: the typed version is the channel, text in and text out; literate is a competence, verbose a style of output. The dropped verbal-thinker of part 3 was nearest; this replaces it.
notes: 'Often addicted' rendered as 'often hooked'. 'PowerPoint' omitted (a brand). Strength: neutral.

label: receiving gifts
source_text: "Don't mistake this love language for materialism; the receiver of gifts thrives on the love, thoughtfulness, and effort behind the gift. If you speak this love language, the perfect gift or gesture shows that you are known, you are cared for, and you are prized above whatever was sacrificed to bring the gift to you. A missed birthday, anniversary, or a hasty, thoughtless gift would be disastrous – so would the absence of everyday gestures. Gifts are visual representations of love and are treasured greatly."
description_draft: This means feeling loved through gifts, treasured for the thought and effort behind them: the right present shows one is known and prized; a forgotten birthday or a hasty gift is disastrous.
nearest_existing: materialistic / sentimental / grateful: the source itself fences off materialistic; sentimental is nearest (the gift as token), but the typed version is the channel of felt love and its wound, not a general sentimentality.
notes: The 'not materialism' defence is carried by 'treasured for the thought and effort behind them' rather than stated. Strength: as the source.

label: Slytherin
source_text: Wizarding World (2021-04-28): "Slytherin house has an unfortunate reputation"; Slytherins are "ambitious, shrewd and possibly destined for greatness"; the kind of person who "is always one step ahead, has a dark sense of humour, thinks reputation is important, takes pride in their appearance and doesn't let anyone see their soft side". Official fact file: Salazar Slytherin's students were "representative of his preference for characters defined by cunning, pride and ambition". Wikipedia: "values ambition, cunning, leadership, and resourcefulness." Official 'house animal and colours' feature: the serpent "often represents cunning; a trait which is very much part of the Slytherin identity."
description_draft: This means being ambitious, shrewd, cunning and proud, always one step ahead, minding one's reputation and appearance, with a dark sense of humor, and never letting anyone see one's soft side.
nearest_existing: ambitious / calculating / scheming / guarded: the typed version is the house portrait, ambition and cunning worn with pride and a guarded front; calculating and scheming carry a dishonesty the source does not state, ambitious lacks the cunning.
notes: The official text softens the house ('unfortunate reputation', 'possibly destined for greatness') relative to the books' Sorting Hat ('those cunning folk use any means to achieve their ends'), which I could not fetch (Fandom 402, Wikiquote lacks the song); the draft mirrors the official text. Markedly more flattering than the corpus's calculating or scheming; Roger may want it sharpened toward the book. 'Possibly destined for greatness' dropped for length. US spelling 'humor'. Fact file: https://www.harrypotter.com/fact-file/magical-miscellany/slytherin.

label: striver (VALS)
source_text: Wikipedia 'VALS' § Segments: "These consumers are the low-resource group of those who are motivated by achievements. They have values very similar to achievers but have fewer economic, social, and psychological resources." Textbook rendering (Brainscape): "are trendy and fun loving. They have little discretionary income and tend to have narrow interests." ThinkInsights: "oriented around status and peer approval, but with far fewer economic and psychological resources to back those ambitions." Umbrex: "Style-conscious, approval-seeking; desire is ahead of means".
description_draft: This means being trendy and fun-loving, wanting status and the approval of others, with ambitions that run ahead of one's money, and buying stylish things that copy what the better-off own.
nearest_existing: status_seeking / materialistic / financially_precarious: the typed version joins the three, the wish for status and approval outrunning the means and spent on style; status_seeking has no money problem, financially_precarious no aspiration.
notes: SBI page unreachable today. SBI's own 'Money defines success for Strivers, who don't have enough of it' and 'see themselves as having a job rather than a career' are known but not quoted. Strength: gently unflattering, as the source; about the corpus's level.

label: survivor (VALS)
source_text: Wikipedia 'VALS' § Segments: "These consumers have the lowest incomes. They have too few resources to be included in any consumer self-orientation and are thus located below the rectangle." Textbook rendering (Brainscape): "lead narrowly focused lives. Because they have the fewest resources, they do not exhibit a primary motivation and often feel powerless." slm.mba: "Their lives are focused on meeting basic needs rather than fulfilling broader desires." Umbrex: "Risk-averse, brand-loyal within constraints; value price and familiarity; need reassurance and simplicity."
description_draft: This means leading a narrow life on the fewest means, meeting needs rather than wants, often feeling powerless, prizing safety and familiarity, and buying cautiously, loyal to known brands and low prices.
nearest_existing: poor / cautious / risk_averse / brand_loyal: the typed version is the whole low-resource life, needs over wants, safety and the familiar, cautious loyal buying; poor is the circumstance alone, cautious the temperament alone.
notes: SBI page unreachable today. SBI's own 'often believe that the world is changing too quickly' and 'loyal to favorite brands, especially if they can purchase them at a discount' were seen in search snippets, not on a fetchable page. 'Often feel powerless' kept as 'often'. Strength: unflattering-sympathetic, as the source; the only VALS member that is plainly a hardship portrait.

label: thinker (VALS)
source_text: Wikipedia 'VALS' § Segments: "These consumers are the high-resource group of those who are motivated by ideals. They are mature, responsible, well-educated professionals." Textbook rendering (Brainscape): "are mature satisfied, comfortable and reflective. They tend to be well educated and actively seek out information in the decision making process." slm.mba: "mature, reflective, and well-informed individuals with high resources. They value quality, durability, and functionality." ThinkInsights: "favor information-rich media, and stay informed about broader social, scientific and business developments."
description_draft: This means being a mature, comfortable, reflective and well-educated person guided by ideals, valuing order, knowledge and responsibility, reading up before any decision, and buying for durability, function and value over show.
nearest_existing: deliberate / educated / cerebral / practical: the typed version is the comfortable, informed professional who buys sensibly; deliberate is the decision style alone, educated the attainment alone, with no ideals clause or buying habit.
notes: SBI page unreachable today. SBI's own 'value order, knowledge, and responsibility' (confirmed in a search-engine snippet, not on a fetched page) is used in the draft; 'moderate respect for the status quo' and 'open to consider new ideas' are known but not quoted. Strength: flattering (mature, reflective, sensible); markedly more flattering than the corpus's plain cerebral or deliberate.

label: visual (VARK)
source_text: "The Visual preference includes the depiction of information in maps, diagrams, charts, graphs, flow charts, and all the symbolic arrows, circles, hierarchies, and other devices, that people use to represent what could have been presented in words." It does NOT include still pictures or photographs of reality, movies, videos, or PowerPoint; it encompasses "designs, white space, patterns, shapes, and the different formats that are used to highlight and convey information."
description_draft: This means taking in information best as maps, diagrams, charts, graphs, flow charts and symbolic arrows and hierarchies, in layout, pattern and shape, rather than in words, photographs or video.
nearest_existing: figurative / big_picture / conceptual: none is about the channel; the dropped visual-thinker of part 3 was nearest and this replaces it, with Fleming's narrower sense (diagrams, not pictures).
notes: The 'rather than' clause is kept because 'visual' is polysemous and Fleming's exclusion of photographs and video picks the sense. Strength: neutral.

label: words of affirmation
source_text: "Actions don't always speak louder than words. If this is your love language, unsolicited compliments mean the world to you. Hearing the words, 'I love you,' is important – hearing the reasons behind that love sends your spirits skyward. Insults can leave you shattered and are not easily forgotten. Kind, encouraging, and positive words are truly life-giving."
description_draft: This means feeling loved through words: an unprompted compliment means the world, hearing why one is loved sends the spirits soaring, and an insult shatters and is not easily forgotten.
nearest_existing: thin_skinned / encouraging / effusive: encouraging and effusive are about giving words; thin_skinned shares the wound but not the delight; the typed version is the channel of received love.
notes: 'Can leave you shattered' -> 'shatters'. Strength: as the source. Length 30, within the set's 30 to 32.
